85 year old man. brought to the ED for persistent back pain. Patient
   was noted to be hyptensive and given fliud. X-rays of spine and knee
   (recent fall onto left knee) were negative for acute abnormalities. UA
   was concering for infection. Was started on cipro. Then was noted to
   have change in mental status. Electrolytes showed Na 122. Patient was
   given 2 liters of NS and then 50 cc of hypertonic saline with
   improvement in mental status.  Repeat electrolytes showed Na=126. Head
   CT negative for acute processes.  Body CT negative for new pathology.
   Hypotension (not Shock)
   Assessment:
   b/p 80/51, as low as 65/45 pt appeared to be sleeping, easily aroused
   w/voice and able to answer orientation ?s appropriately. As pt has
   documented hypotension plan in ICU is to rx for symptomatic hypotension
   and encourage Pos. Started on Cipro for UTI, noted foley catheter not
   from [**Hospital1 5**] so foley catheter changed using aseptic technique and no
   apparent complications, UA, c&s sent.
   Action:
   Awoken easily  when hypotensive, MDs in to eval when hypotensive to
   65/45
   Response:
   Hypotensive ? contributing factor w/change in MS
   [**Name13 (STitle) 99**]:
   Continue to monitor b/p, rx for symptomatic b/p as has hx of sbp 80,
   encourage PO intake
   .H/O altered mental status (not Delirium)
   Assessment:
   Oriented to self, place & time, however, unable to identify
   careproviders as such. Noted sudden onset of expressive and receptive
   aphasia, emergent head CT done which was
 for bleed. Then noted
   transient expressive aphasia which was as frequent as every
 hour and
   was also noted with neurology team. Last Na 136
   Action:
   Reorient PRN, provide safe environment, frequent neuro checks
   Response:
   Reorients easily, does notice word search difficulty and garbled speech
   Plan:
   Hx of falls, placed on fall precautions, frequent checks to ensure
   safety, call light and necessary objects in reach. Q1-2hour neuro
   checks. MRI done 1800. Family kept up to date and informed. Wife and
   dtr at bedside. Q8hour Na+ checks, due @ 2200. Neuro diff:
   encephalopathy d/t electrolyte/fluid abnormality. f/u w/MRI results.
   Pain control (acute pain, chronic pain)
   Assessment:
   Pt denies pain, had refused Tylenol early this morning but did take
   with morning medications
   Action:
   Tylenol q6hour for pain, held this afternoon with neurologic changes
   Response:
   Denies pain
   Plan:
   Continue to assess for pain, medicate as ordered w/Tylenol RTC and
   oxycodone PRN

Document 2, written later in the same hospitalization, notes that the patient’s CIWA has fallen to 8 after treatment. This reflects the expected clinical improvement of withdrawal symptoms with benzodiazepine therapy, not a mutually exclusive fact. The discrepancy is therefore an ordinary disease‑course evolution rather than a true contradiction.

**Clinical Significance Score:** 2  
**Temporal Appropriatenes:** 1  

**Overall Score:** (1 + 2 + 1) ÷ 3 ≈ 1.3 (rounded to 1)

   CAD, s/p CABG/stents , s/p AVR/MVR, HTN, hypercholestrol, GERD, s/p
   choleycystectomy admitted in MWH  on [**9-17**] with c/o N/V and acute
   abdominal pain. CT showed gall stones as per report pt was febrile to
   101.4 and hypotensive with SBP  79. Pt did receive fluid bolus 500  ml
   X 3 prior to admission to [**Hospital1 54**].
   [**Date range (1) 9961**]  pt received 7 liters LR fluid boluses without improvement in
   UO or BP overnight. A-line was placed in left radial. Triple lumen CVL
   placed in right IJ.  Pt required levophed for hypotension. He had
   increasing O2 requirement with insp/exp wheezes and c/o SOB.  Lactate
   was up to 2.9. Treated with small doses of morphine for pain.
   ERCP was done [**9-19**]. Pus, sludge and stones were removed from CBD and
   stent was placed. Tolerated procedure well. Extubated in MICU post
   procedure and weaned to 2L NC. Levophed switched to Vasopressin
   2.4u/hr.  Creatinine remained elevated at 2.8 but UO did improve post
   ERCP. Abdominal pain improved and pt
s vitals were stable.
   Cholangitis
   Assessment:
   Admitted [**2151-9-18**] with cholangitis from [**Hospital3 1596**]. Required a-line,
   central line and pressors for septic picture. WBC peaked at 16.9.
   Action:
   Treated with antibiotics and ERCP done [**2151-9-19**] to remove pus, stones and
   insert stent. Intubated for procedure. Extubated post procedure and
   weaned to 2L N/C.
   Response:
   WBC down to 6.0 today. Vital signs stable overnight on vasopressin. CVP
   14-18 Remains dyspneic and wheezy with minimal exertion. O2 sats and
   ABG are good.
   Plan:
   Continue antibiotics. Vasopressin was stopped earlier today and if
   stable could go to floor. ?may need lasix for wheezes if BP tolerates
   it since he is volume overloaded from fluid rescucitation.
   Renal failure, acute (Acute renal failure, ARF)
   Assessment:
   Admitted with creatinine 2.7 on [**2151-9-18**] and peaked at 2.8. Team thinks
   possible ATN from hypotension/sepsis.
   Action:
   Fluids and pressors given over the past 24hrs with improved UO and
   creatinine down to 2.5 today.
   Response:
   UO 40-100cc/hr over night. Electrolytes within normal limits.
   Plan:
   Continue to follow vital signs and UO as well as lytes and renal
   function.

Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH)
   Assessment:
          t max 100
          HR tachycardic to 130
s, self cardioverted into NSR ~ 2100
   after Esmolol discontinued and Amiodarone had not been started.
          Neuro status unchanged, no spontaneous movement, minimal
   withdrawl to nail bed pressure, no withdrawl of right upper extremity.
          Pupils equal and reactive to light
          goal SBP 110-140, pt hypertensive during shift
          ventriculostomy drain x2 @ 15 mm / hg above tragus with
   ICP
s ~10
          On ventilator AC, spontaneously breathing over vent with a
   respiratory alkalosis present.
   Action:
          Hydralazine and Lopressor given
          Nicardipine drip started
          Neuro eval q 1 hour
   Response:
          HR NSR rate controlled in the 80
          blood pressure goals met
          neuro status remains concerning, unchanged
   Plan:
          continue frequent monitoring of neuro status
          continue to meet goal SBP of 110-140
          continue ventriculostomy drains
          emotional support for family
          planned family meeting for Monday morning to re-evaluate
   plan of care

   pt
s husband, 3 sons and pt
s sister.  Family notified of finding of

s current plan of care.  Family

s current condition

   significant injury to the brain.  Pt
s sons are good advocates for

   was functioning remarkably well prior to this event.
   Pt
s twin sister appears to be having the most difficulty coping with
   the possibility of a less than successful outcome.  Sister is supported
   by her 3 daughters who have been here with her daily.
   Will continue to follow pt
s progress and provide support to family.

[**2137-9-6**] 1:23 PM
 CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST                                            Clip # [**Clip Number (Radiology) 91055**]
 Reason: concern for acute mental status change in patient with bilia
 Admitting Diagnosis: END STAGE LIVER DISEASE
 ______________________________________________________________________________
 [**Hospital 4**] MEDICAL CONDITION:
  56yM with HCV/HCC s/p cyberknife, now s/p OLT [**2137-8-30**]. [**8-31**]: cordis removed, TLC
  placed over RIJ line. 56yM with HCV/HCC s/p cyberknife, now s/p OLT [**2137-8-30**].  Pt
  decompensated on floor [**9-4**] (desat), pt with necrotic segment of Liver, with
  large amounts Bile outputs.[**9-5**]: Pt had ERCP. Pt with hypoxia post procedure of
  unclear etiology. Return to SICU, aggitiated, but sat improved.
 REASON FOR THIS EXAMINATION:
  concern for acute mental status change in patient with biliary anastomotic leak
  after OLT
 No contraindications for IV contrast
 ______________________________________________________________________________
 PROVISIONAL FINDINGS IMPRESSION (PFI): AJy FRI [**2137-9-6**] 6:26 PM
  PFI:  No acute intracranial process.
 ______________________________________________________________________________
                                 FINAL REPORT
 HISTORY:  56-year-old male with altered mental status.

 COMPARISON:  None.

 TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images were obtained through the brain without
 administration of IV contrast.

 FINDINGS:  There is mild sulcal enlargement consistent with mild global
 atrophy.  There is no evidence for hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or
 infarction.  The [**Doctor Last Name 181**]-white matter differentiation is preserved.  There is no
 effacement of the cisterns.  The osseous structures are unremarkable.  The
 paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.

 IMPRESSION:  Mild global atrophy.  No evidence for acute intracranial process.

[**2137-9-6**] 1:23 PM
 CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST                                            Clip # [**Clip Number (Radiology) 91055**]
 Reason: concern for acute mental status change in patient with bilia
 Admitting Diagnosis: END STAGE LIVER DISEASE
 ______________________________________________________________________________
 [**Hospital 4**] MEDICAL CONDITION:
  56yM with HCV/HCC s/p cyberknife, now s/p OLT [**2137-8-30**]. [**8-31**]: cordis removed, TLC
  placed over RIJ line. 56yM with HCV/HCC s/p cyberknife, now s/p OLT [**2137-8-30**].  Pt
  decompensated on floor [**9-4**] (desat), pt with necrotic segment of Liver, with
  large amounts Bile outputs.[**9-5**]: Pt had ERCP. Pt with hypoxia post procedure of
  unclear etiology. Return to SICU, aggitiated, but sat improved.
 REASON FOR THIS EXAMINATION:
  concern for acute mental status change in patient with biliary anastomotic leak
  after OLT
 No contraindications for IV contrast
 ______________________________________________________________________________
 PROVISIONAL FINDINGS IMPRESSION (PFI): AJy FRI [**2137-9-6**] 6:26 PM
  PFI:  No acute intracranial process.
 ______________________________________________________________________________
                                 FINAL REPORT
 HISTORY:  56-year-old male with altered mental status.

 COMPARISON:  None.

 TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images were obtained through the brain without
 administration of IV contrast.

 FINDINGS:  There is mild sulcal enlargement consistent with mild global
 atrophy.  There is no evidence for hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or
 infarction.  The [**Doctor Last Name 181**]-white matter differentiation is preserved.  There is no
 effacement of the cisterns.  The osseous structures are unremarkable.  The
 paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.

 IMPRESSION:  Mild global atrophy.  No evidence for acute intracranial process.

  abnormalities.

  lung disease unchanged. Trace dependent aerosolized material in bronchus
  intermedius without other acute airway abnormalities.

                                 FINAL REPORT
 INDICATION:  46-year-old man with hemoptysis and shortness of breath and
 tachycardia, recent gastric banding in 01/[**2181**].  Additional history of alpha-1
 antitrypsin deficiency.

 COMPARISON:  CT chest of [**2180-3-16**].

 TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the chest before
 and after the administration of intravenous contrast material.  Multiplanar
 reformatted images were generated.

 CT CHEST WITHOUT AND WITH IV CONTRAST:  The pulmonary arterial tree is
 suboptimally opacified. Allowing for this, there is no evidence of pulmonary
 embolism. Subsegmental vessels are not fully assessed. The aorta is normal in
 caliber throughout, without mucosal abnormality.

 Within the mediastinum and hila, there are again multiple prominent lymph
 nodes, the largest located in the right hilum measuring up to 14 mm in short
 axis (3:65).  Multiple precarinal and prevascular lymph nodes are not
 significantly changed.  The heart size is normal without clear evidence of
 right heart strain.

 Lung findings are stable when compared to [**2180-2-25**] exam.  Again, there is
 extensive bronchiectasis demonstrating a basilar predominant involvement.
 Saccular bronchiectasis again demonstrates wall thickening and multiple air-
 fluid levels at the right lung base. Emphysema throughout both lungs are
 again noted consistent with history of alpha-1 antitrypsin deficient
 status. Again, there are multiple pulmonary nodules scattered throughout the
 region of bronchiectasis. Previously noted nodules are largely unchanged.  A
 nodule in the lingula (3:53) measures 5 mm, previously 4 mm, likely a
 technical difference.  There is no new consolidation, pleural effusion or

 pneumothorax.

 While this exam is not tailored for evaluation of the abdomen, the patient is
 post-gastric banding surgery, with hardware intact in the epigastrium.  The
 liver is shrunken and nodular in contour, again consistent with cirrhosis.
 Splenomegaly is again noted.  There is no free fluid in the abdomen.
 Retroperitoneal varices are again noted.

 OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  Degenerative changes are again present in the thoracic
 spine, with an anterior wedge compression deformity unchanged in T6 vertebral
 body.  There is no new fracture or worrisome lytic or sclerotic bony lesions.
 Soft tissues are notable for gynecomastia, but are otherwise unremarkable.

 IMPRESSION:
 1.  No evidence of PE. or acute aortic process.
 2.  Stable extensive bronchiectasis, with regions of saccular bronchiectasis
 and air-fluid levels and wall thickening in the right lower lobe.  Stable
 emphysema.
 3.  Unchanged pulmonary nodules. Recommend attention to these areas on f/u
 exams.
 4.  Cirrhotic liver with splenomegaly.
